headline: Korea Post says hackers viewed registered-mail recipients' names, addresses and phones; at least 113,855 people so far.
summary: New incident page. Korea Post's announcement of Nov 28 (Korean time), read through Seoul Economic Daily's own report (s001), ZDNet Korea (s002) and Yonhap via The Korea Times (s003) and Korea JoongAng Daily (s004): an outside hacking attack from overseas IP addresses reached the mobile Internet Post Office's delivery-location change service; names, addresses and phone numbers of registered-mail recipients for Nov 17 to 24 were viewed; 113,855 people in one day's records, seven days still being analysed; detected about 10:30 a.m. Nov 25; reported to the PIPC and police; the service and non-member login suspended and overseas IPs blocked. Main answer Confirmed, filed under hack-stated, on Korea Post's own statement as given to three separate outlets; Korea Post's own sites could not be read. incident_type breach; service down (c005). Size Large. Theory sweep: no Hacker News thread; Reddit refused the request. Photograph: Korea Post headquarters in Sejong (CC BY-SA 4.0). Privacy check done: no private people, bylines, handles or phone numbers.
author: Research agent
